jess-cs: Hey team, escalated ticket from Acme — running Redwood Private in a customer VPC. They started seeing API 403s to model-registry and failures installing wheels from pypi; also our telemetry events are not arriving. They say it worked yesterday. Can we triage?

maria-support: Thanks Jess. Can you paste the minimal repro and the exact error payloads? Is this only in their private deployment or also hitting hosted?

jess-cs: Private-only. Customer sent curl output and pip error. Short snippets:
```
$ curl -v https://model-registry.internal.redwood:443/v1/models/foo
* Connected to model-registry.internal.redwood (10.0.3.12) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection using ...
> GET /v1/models/foo HTTP/1.1
> Host: model-registry.internal.redwood
< HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
< content-type: application/json
< date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 14:02:39 GMT
{"error":"access_denied","detail":"token rejected from auth service"}
```

And pip fails pulling a wheel: 
```
Collecting redwood-runtime
  Retrying (retrying...): Could not fetch URL https://files.pythonhosted.org/... - <urlopen error [SSL: UNKNOWN_PROTOCOL] unknown protocol (_ssl.c:... )>
```

jess-cs: They also forwarded agent logs showing telemetry POSTs 502/timed out: `POST https://telemetry.redwood-internal/api/v1/events -> connection reset`

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-20250911-9987 (priority: P2)

maria-support: Ok — sounds like egress/TLS/DNS issues. Alex, can infra confirm what hosts and ports customers need whitelisted for Private/VPC installs? We should give them a minimal allowlist for pypi, model pulls, auth, telemetry, and KMS.

alex-infra: Yep. Typical root causes: corporate egress proxy, split-horizon DNS returning internal IPs, or SNI/transparent TLS MITM dropping connections. For this customer we need them to check NAT + firewall + proxy. Minimal hosts and FQDNs (port 443) to allow: 
- api.redwood.ai (control plane - auth/token endpoints)
- model-registry.internal.redwood (model manifests & shards)
- storage-models.redwood-cdn.net (model shard CDN endpoints)
- telemetry.redwood-internal (metrics/events ingestion)
- pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org (pip)
- artifactory.acme.internal (if they mirror packages)
- kms.us-east-1.amazonaws.com (if using AWS KMS)

alex-infra: Also recommend allowing SNI passthrough for those TLS hosts. If their proxy does TLS interception, ensure the proxy has the CA we ship preloaded or that they bypass interception for these hosts.

maria-support: Can we give them quick commands to reproduce/diagnose?

sean-mlops: Provide these checks: 
1) DNS resolution from the private subnet: `dig +short model-registry.internal.redwood @<their-dns>` -> should return private loadbalancer IPs (not corporate web proxy IPs).
2) TLS handshake check: `openssl s_client -connect model-registry.internal.redwood:443 -servername model-registry.internal.redwood` — look for `Verify return code: 0 (ok)` and the full cert chain.
3) Curl with verbose to see TLS/SNI and response: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://model-registry.internal.redwood/v1/models/foo`
4) Pip test: `python -m pip install -vvv --no-cache-dir redwood-runtime` and capture the SSL error.

maria-support: Jess, can you ask the customer to run those three and paste outputs? Also confirm if they have an egress proxy (Zscaler/BlueCoat) or NGFW.

jess-cs: On it. I also asked for a traceroute/NAT gateway info. They replied: "We do have Zscaler in this VPC path via corporate shared-VPC."

alex-infra: zscaler often does TLS break with SNI mismatches for split-horizon. If their DNS returns internal LB IPs but the proxy expects external hostnames, you'll see TLS protocol errors or 403 from our auth. For immediate unblock, ask them to bypass interception for the redwood hosts and allow CONNECT passthrough to port 443.

maria-support: Also flagging the billing side — if telemetry isn't flowing our usage might under-report which can affect invoices. Ops: we should note this customer as "data incomplete" while they resolve.

oncall-bot: Pager duty: on-call infra acknowledged INC-20250911-9987

sean-mlops: If they still see 403 from model-registry after TLS is confirmed, we should check token exchange logs. Ask them to curl the auth endpoint: `curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/token -d 'grant_type=client_credentials' -u client:secret` — ensure token fetch succeeds. If token fetch fails, it's auth egress to api.redwood.ai being blocked.

maria-support: Good. I've drafted an allowlist KB for customers that I'll paste here after we confirm their repro. For now summary to send: 
• Allow TLS egress (443) to api.redwood.ai, model-registry.internal.redwood, storage-models.redwood-cdn.net, telemetry.redwood-internal, pypi.org, files.pythonhosted.org, and their KMS.
• Ensure proxy bypass or SNI passthrough for those hosts.
• Run diagnostics: dig, openssl s_client, curl -v, pip -vvv, auth token curl.
• If using an internal package mirror, whitelist that mirror domain too.

jess-cs: Customer ran checks, attaching results: dig returns internal LB IPs, openssl shows cert signed by corporate CA (not our expected public cert), pip still failing with SSL UNKNOWN_PROTOCOL. They say they can't bypass Zscaler at the moment.

alex-infra: That matches a TLS MITM. Either they add the corporate CA to trust store for their agent runtime or we advise a bypass for the redwood hosts. For long term, we can provide an option to configure a proxy/pac in the installer (we already have env vars: HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY), but note TLS interception will still alter certs and may break mTLS or token validation.

maria-support: OK. Next steps: Jess -> ask customer to either allow passthrough for the listed hosts OR add corporate CA to host trust store and to the python/agent CA bundle. Also request token fetch logs if they try the auth curl. I'll mark the ticket as "waiting on customer" and attach our diagnostic checklist.

jess-cs: Sent checklist. Customer acknowledged and will try bypass. Will update when they confirm. :thumbsup:
